newIssues.title: Version tiles grow to their label's width, so the ⋯ floats off the thumbnail at ≤1024 and the tiles are unevenly spaced
newIssues.repro: Open Kevin Ng › Living room at 768×1024 with touch and look at the versions strip (V2 and V3).
newIssues.evidence: Measured tile vs image vs ⋯. At 768: Original tile 89–198 over a 96px image (89–185); V2 tile 318–426 (image 318–414), ⋯ 398–422; V3 tile 438–571 (image 438–534), ⋯ 543–567, entirely off the image. At 390 the V3 ⋯ is at 284–308 while the image ends at 275. At 1440 the V3 tile is 133 on a 128 image. `.tile { flex: 0 0 128px }` / `flex-basis: 96px` keep the default min-width:auto, so the nowrap label ('V3 · Relit · Golden Hour', min-content 133px) widens the tile. The ⋯ is pinned to the tile's top-right (the F005 move), so it hangs in the gap between tiles, and the gaps between thumbnails vary. The label's ellipsis never triggers. It also carries only a native title, which the UI sweep rules out for information.
newIssues.fix: In versions-strip.module.css give `.tile` `min-width: 0` (or `width: 128px` / `96px` at ≤1024) so it stays the image's width and `.label` ellipsizes. Anchor `.kebab` to `.open` (the thumbnail) rather than the tile. The full label is already in the button's aria-label. For sighted users, put it in a house Tooltip on the label instead of `title`.

newIssues.title: The changes list's 'more below' fade shows on every list, so the last chip always dissolves at its bottom edge
newIssues.repro: On a design at 1440, pick one finish (or three changes). Look at the chips above Generate.
newIssues.evidence: ChangeChips reports scrollHeight − clientHeight = 4px whatever the count: 1 chip gives 32/28, 2 chips 32/28, 3 chips 68/64. So `data-more` is always set, and the 20px mask fades the last row's bottom border and text. In p14-three.png the 'Your note ×' chip loses its bottom edge although nothing is hidden, and p5-during.png shows the same. The 4px overflow also lets the list jiggle 4px on the wheel.
newIssues.fix: Find the 4px overflow: the × button's hit area (`.changeX` / its tooltip wrapper) or the chip's outline extends past the chip. Clip it (`overflow: clip` on `.change`, or keep the hit area inside the 28px). Alternatively, give the check a tolerance: `scrollTop + clientHeight < scrollHeight - 6`, or compare against the last chip's bottom. The fade should appear only when a whole chip row is hidden.

newIssues.evidence: [data-testid=render-share] (.page) measures 718 px wide at every width from 768 to 1440, while its parent, PageReveal's .content, fills the viewport. results.evidence: Editor 1440, draft pin: typed 'Test note by verifier', pressed Esc in the textarea, and the draft count went to 0. Thread: typed in Reply, pressed Esc, and the thread count went to 0. Client link 1440: Esc in the draft's box gave draft count 0 (j-client.cjs).

Fixed: after a keyboard Generate, focus lands on the running card's Cancel at 80ms. Fixed: once the save starts, focus moves to the run card DIV. Fixed: a thread opened from its pin returns focus to that pin on Close.

Not fixed, after a run: when it lands, focus falls to BODY. Trace (a-gen2.cjs): 4031ms Cancel → 5693 BODY → 5710 run-card DIV → 5941 BODY once the card detached. The new V-tile never gets focus.

Not fixed, after Cancel: pressing Cancel during a run also leaves focus on BODY (x-cancel.cjs: [0 Cancel] [229 BODY]), not on Generate.

Not fixed, pins: draft Cancel or Esc returns focus to BODY, whether the draft was opened with the mouse or with Enter on the photo. After Pin it, the thread takes focus, but Esc in its Reply box leaves focus on BODY. After 'Remove the pin', focus is on BODY (b-pin.cjs, r-kbdpin.cjs).

Root causes:
(1) The focus-after-run effect in visualizer-editor.tsx (~l.273-285) returns early when activeElement is inside rootRef and not disabled. The exiting run card, which AnimatePresence keeps mounted for about 200ms, still holds focus, so the effect gives up. The card then unmounts and focus falls to BODY.
(2) FloatCard's useDialogFocus (pin-card.tsx l.99, surface.ts l.61) records `previous` in an effect. That effect runs after NoteBox's autoFocus, so the draft's stored 'opener' is its own textarea, which is gone on unmount. For the thread that opens right after a save, the opener is BODY.
results.remaining:
- **After a run or a cancel:** treat focus inside [data-testid=viz-running] as idle. Alternatively, move focus in AnimatePresence's onExitComplete, so it lands on the new V-tile after a run and on Generate after a cancel.
- **Pins:** record the opener in the editor when a draft or thread opens (the photo region, the pin toggle, or the pin marker). Restore it on Cancel, Esc, Save and Close. After Save, return to the new pin's marker. After Remove, fall back to the pin toggle. Don't rely on useDialogFocus capturing it after autoFocus.

newIssues.title: Undo on Change photo within the same second leaves the new photo showing, under the old reading and picks
newIssues.repro: On a room with no versions, make a pick, then choose Room options › Change photo › pick a JPG. Press the snackbar's Undo right away (within about 1 s). Reload.
newIssues.evidence: t90b: after Undo, the canvas and the Original tile still show the new photo (the kitchen mood board), with the old photo's marked surfaces and the 'Walls → Terracotta' pick on top of it, and a reload does not fix it. The DB holds the restored photo, and a fresh browser context shows it correctly. roomImage uses `?v=${updatedAt.getTime()}`, a whole-second timestamp. setRoomPhoto and undoRoomPhoto in the same second produce the same address, and /visualizer/img/room is served `private, max-age=31536000, immutable`, so the browser keeps the new photo under that address. With a 2.5 s pause Undo works. updatedAt also moves on every autosave, so each save gives the photo a new address and forces a re-download.
newIssues.fix: Version the room picture by its content, not by the row's updatedAt. For example, store a photo hash or photo revision set only by addRoom, setRoomPhoto and undoRoomPhoto, and build roomImage from it.

newIssues.title: Dusk and night lights lay a hard-edged navy box over the windows that cuts through the sofa, curtains and sill decor
newIssues.repro: Any sample room, Original, Lighting, Blue Hour (also Warm Cozy Home). Look at the preview or the generated version.
newIssues.evidence: Living room: a flat navy quadrilateral covers the window. Its right edge is a straight vertical at x≈0.218 that cuts the sheer curtain and tints the sofa's back cushion inside the box (t22-zoom-sofa-box.png). Master bedroom V2 · Relit · Blue Hour: the box covers the frame and the left sheer, and its right edge slices through the pampas vase on the sill (t6-06-window-zoom.png). Kitchen: the window box, plus a floating blue rectangle at the top right (0.93–1 × 0.15–0.205) with nothing behind it (t22-Kitchen-Blue-Hour.png). The cause is grade.ts, which replaces pixels inside hand-traced quads (SAMPLE_LIGHT windows in lighting.ts) using an unfeathered polygonMask, with nothing that stands in front of the window taken out.
newIssues.fix: In grade.ts, key the sky on the glass: within the quad, weight by the pixel's daylight luminance so frames, curtains and objects keep their tone. Feather the mask (spreadMask/blur) and subtract the room's furniture cutouts. In lighting.ts, retrace the living-room and bedroom quads to the glass only, and drop or retrace the kitchen's second quad.

newIssues.title: A pick or un-pick made less than a second before a reload or tab close is still lost

newIssues.evidence: The hint reads 'Essentials plus a few extras — lived-in Places what the sample room holds; how much furniture follows in the full release.' The density hint has no full stop, so it runs into the next sentence, and 'follows in the full release' is roadmap talk. The note under it still says 'Furnishing works on an emptied room: empty it first.' on V3, which is already empty.
newIssues.fix: In tools-panel.tsx line 70, join with '. ' and drop the release sentence. On line 74, show 'empty it first' only when the version is not emptied (finishes.emptied).

newIssues.title: The Tools tab shows a 'has changes' dot when the only change is a typed note
newIssues.repro: On a version with no picks, open Lighting and type 'a darker rug' in Describe a change.
newIssues.evidence: The dock's Tools tab gets its dot ('Tools, has changes') even though nothing in Tools was touched. On a phone the note box sits above every panel. marks.tools = !!pending.tool || !!pending.note.trim().
newIssues.fix: Mark Tools only for pending.tool. The note is already counted in 'n changes' and has its own row in the changes sheet.

newIssues.title: Adding the same version to a quote again silently makes a second new quote
newIssues.repro: Gerald Tan's design › V1 ⋯ › Add to a quote… › Add to quote (creates OM-10010). Open it again: the dialog preselects 'A new quote'. Tapping Add to quote creates OM-10011 with the same two lines.
newIssues.evidence: INTO shows 'OM-10010 · Gerald Tan' and 'A new quote' (selected), with no word that OM-10010 already holds V1. The DB then has two draft quotes with identical 'Living room · V1 finishes' sections. QuoteDialog defaults to drafts.find(q => !holds(q)) ?? 'new'.
newIssues.fix: When a draft already holds this version, say so on its chip and in a line under INTO ('OM-10010 already has V1'). Don't preselect 'A new quote' silently: preselect nothing, or the holding draft with the 'Add again' label.

newIssues.title: The quote editor at 390 (reached by 'Open quote'): stray '2', clipped Additional Discount, cramped GST and By category rows
newIssues.repro: Add a version to a quote › snackbar Open quote › Items.
newIssues.evidence: A lone '2' (items-table .addNum) floats at the left edge above Add Item. In the totals card, 'Additional Discount' is cut to 'Additional I' under the % select, with a stray 't' between the select and the amount box. 'GST 9%' touches its switch. 'BY CATEGORY · 1 · share of' wraps into the Share / Margin chips.
newIssues.fix: ≤767: hide .addNum in the card layout. Stack the Additional discount row (label on its own line, then the select + amount). Give the GST row a gap. Let the By category head wrap above its chips.

newIssues.title: The Kind sheet on the landing doesn't show which choice is current
newIssues.repro: Tools › AI Visualizer › Kind: All ▾ › Personal › open the pill again.
newIssues.evidence: 'All · 8', 'Leads · 2' and 'Personal · 6' look identical: no check, no bold, no colour. aria-checked is true on Personal, but DropdownItem draws nothing for it and no CSS targets [aria-checked='true']. The same happens in every LibraryGallery scope pill.
newIssues.fix: Give DropdownItem a checked look for menuitemradio/checkbox: a trailing check icon plus primary text (menus.module.css `.item[aria-checked='true']`), so every scope pill and View-by menu shows the current value.

newIssues.title: At 320 the canvas toolbar clips its last button (Download)
newIssues.repro: Open a design at 320×640.
newIssues.evidence: The canvas toolbar measures scrollWidth 321 vs clientWidth 302 (overflow:auto), and the Download icon is cut at the right edge. The sideways scroll has no affordance.
newIssues.fix: ≤359: tighten the toolbar (drop the divider, or 32px buttons), or fold Download into the version ⋯ menu (it is already there) and hide it from the toolbar.

newIssues.title: Company › Materials has no filter by category or finish
newIssues.repro: More › Company › Materials.
newIssues.evidence: The toolbar has New Folder · New · Search · ⋯ only: no scope pill and no Filters. Price book › My Items (the same LibraryGallery) has facets. Materials carry category and finish, and the picker groups by category.
newIssues.fix: Pass `facets` (Category, Finish) and optionally a Linked / Not linked scope `filters` to LibraryGallery in materials-view.tsx.

newIssues.title: The changes sheet's 'Clear all' sits 8px below its title
newIssues.repro: Pick any finish › tap '1 change ⌃'.
newIssues.evidence: Measured midlines: title 'Your changes · 1' at 723, 'Clear all' at 731, close at 725. The Sheet's .headActions has margin-top:2px and holds a 36px text Button beside a 24px title.
newIssues.fix: In sheet.module.css `.headActions { align-self: center; margin-top: 0; }`, or give the text button a compact size so it centres on the title.

newIssues.title: Moodboard: the 'Look and light' line is indented off the column
newIssues.repro: A version with a lighting pick › ⋯ › Moodboard › scroll.
newIssues.evidence: 'Lighting — Warm Cozy Home' starts at x=34 while its head 'LOOK AND LIGHT' and every other block start at x=16. The <ul> keeps padding-left:18px but list-style is none, so the indent has no bullet.
newIssues.fix: moodboard.module.css `.list { padding-left: 0; list-style: none; }`.

newIssues.title: An uploaded room photo is named 'Room 2', not after its file
newIssues.repro: Editor › Add room › browse › sophia-living-room.jpg.
newIssues.evidence: The new room chip reads 'Room 2'. A photo added from the lead's Files keeps its file stem (fileStem), but the upload path at visualizer-editor.tsx:508 passes no name, so addRoom falls back to `Room ${n}`.
newIssues.fix: Pass `name: fileStem(file.name)` (dashes to spaces, e.g. 'Sophia living room') on the upload path.

newIssues.title: Landing cards at 390 truncate every line; two new designs read the same
newIssues.repro: Tools › AI Visualizer.
newIssues.evidence: The 2-up cards read 'Sample · Kitch…', 'Personal · 1 room …', 'Kitchen · edited 3 min …'. Two blank designs made today are both 'Design · 26 Sep' with the same meta, so a studio person can't tell them apart.
newIssues.fix: ≤767: let the card title take two lines, and drop the kind word from the meta when the Kind pill already scopes it. Name blank designs 'Design · 26 Sep, 3:40 pm', or number them ('Design · 26 Sep (2)').

newIssues.title: The bell names an unknown client two ways: 'Your client…' and 'Client…'
